subject.title: Feature Request: Batch API support for background tasks

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor an additive delayed/batch agent-turn contract, and should the first supported caller be isolated cron jobs rather than heartbeats, sessions, and subagents together?
rationale: The existing runtime is oriented around immediate streamed turns; selecting the public contract, provider scope, fallback policy, and first caller determines compatibility and cannot be safely inferred from the request alone.

options.title: Sponsor a cron-first delayed-turn design
options.body: Define an additive provider and Plugin SDK lifecycle, then implement an opt-in isolated-cron path with explicit completion, cancellation, delivery, and billing semantics.

options.title: Route the capability outside core
options.body: Decline a core runtime contract until a plugin can implement the feature entirely through existing public seams.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Keep this tracker open without implementation until provider priorities and operator demand justify the cross-cutting lifecycle work.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a cron-first delayed-turn design
recommendation.body: Define an additive provider and Plugin SDK lifecycle, then implement an opt-in isolated-cron path with explicit completion, cancellation, delivery, and billing semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to the provider-runtime and cron decision surfaces.
